You want the `check: true` kwarg to run_command, because recent versions of Meson emit a deprecation warning if you don't specify some value of `check`.

It's best to use "true", because that would ideally have been the default all along -- if those commands error out for some crazy reason Meson can error out if the information is required.

If you're going to use Meson's documented support for f-strings, which was added in Meson 0.58, you might want to set that in the `project()` function as `meson_version: '>=0.58.0'` so that Meson can error out on older versions and tell the user to "upgrade Meson".

It's a pretty recent version and e.g. not available in Debian stable's official repositories. It's of course trivial to upgrade it with `pip install`, but it's quite easy to imagine people trying the version from the Debian repositories first, then having it fail, so letting them know the reason is because they have an old version of Meson is useful information.

I'll try to explain my changes and how I think they relate to the formula above. But all my changes revolve around : add a scaling factor where needed in already existing code / computation formulas.

The original code is (if the window is X11) :

```
local = g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() - m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_vRealPosition.goalv();
```

I understand `g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal()` as `coords`.
I understand `m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_vRealPosition.goalv()` as `windowpos`.

I scaled this whole expression by `m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_fX11SurfaceScaledBy` which I understand as `scale`.

The result is : 

```
local = (g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() - m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_vRealPosition.goalv()) * m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_fX11SurfaceScaledBy;
```

Which corresponds to `(coords - windowpos) * scale` in my understanding. After several tests it works for the initial touch down, which is what this function is all about. 

However this function also prepares another, for touch moves, and stores a `touchSurfaceOrigin`. 

The original code uses two distincts paths if the window is X11 or not to compute the `local` variable. In the X11 case this variable units are X11 scaled units, in the other case the units are global screen scale units. What is important is that they differ.

The original code modifies this variable this way : 

```
m_sTouchData.touchSurfaceOrigin = g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() - local;
```

As `getMouseCoordsInternal()` is in global screen scale units and local may be in one or the other unit, I was forced to compute `touchSurfaceOrigin` differently in the two cases.

The modified code in the case if an X11 window becomes : 

```
m_sTouchData.touchSurfaceOrigin = (g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() * m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_fX11SurfaceScaledBy) - local;
```

`local` is already in X11 units, I have to change the coords again accordingly. (or use a variable and scale it once and for all, but I chose to modify the original code as few as possible). 

All this code prepares what will happen next in `onTouchMove()` that I describe in the other conversation.

The original code is : 

```
const auto local = g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() - m_sTouchData.touchSurfaceOrigin;
```

I changed it to take into account the case where the window is X11 : 

```
 auto local = g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() - m_sTouchData.touchSurfaceOrigin;
 if (m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_bIsX11) {
      local = (g_pInputManager->getMouseCoordsInternal() * m_sTouchData.touchFocusWindow->m_fX11SurfaceScaledBy) - m_sTouchData.touchSurfaceOrigin;
}
```

All I do is to scale anew `getMouseCoordsInternal()` to X11 units. The origin has already been scaled to these units in `onTouchDown`. This could be refactored to avoid computing `local` twice, but once again I wanted to introduce as few changes as possible.
